Getting rid of a hump and saving your neck and back in just 10 minutes a day

An osteopath from China with extensive experience has shown simple exercises for tired and hunched workers. You need to do them with a small pillow or fitness block, whichever is more convenient for you:

1. Place the pillow vertically and move your head from side to side. Do 20 reps on each side, 3 sets.

2. Rest your forehead on the pillow and lift your head, holding at the farthest point. Do 3 sets of 20 reps.

3. Lie on the pillow with your right and left ear, as if turning over in your sleep. Do 3 sets of 20 reps on each side.

4. Then place your chin on the pillow and gently stretch your neck. Hold for 3 sets of 1 minute each.

The complex takes no more than 10 minutes, but after two weeks of regular exercise, the hump and neck strain will disappear, and the blood flow to the head will significantly improve.

A must-have for office workers and remote workers - let's take care of ourselves.

📌 Crypto Options: Buying Insurance on Price Moves

Main Points
⏺ Crypto options give you the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price
⏺ They’re used for hedging, income, and directional bets with defined risk
⏺ This post explains how options differ from simple spot or futures trades

1️⃣ Calls & Puts — call options give you the right to buy at a strike price, puts give you the right to sell at a strike price.
2️⃣ Premium — you pay an upfront fee (premium) for that right; if you don’t use it, the option can expire worthless.
3️⃣ Hedging — options can cap downside (buying puts) or lock in upside (selling calls against a position).
4️⃣ DeFi Options — on-chain protocols let you buy, sell, and structure options with smart contracts instead of brokers.
5️⃣ Defined Risk — unlike leveraged futures, your max loss as an option buyer is the premium you paid.

Final Thoughts

Crypto options turn “all or nothing” price bets into flexible strategies — more tools to shape your risk instead of just hoping the chart goes your way.

📌 Zcash sets July 28 hard fork to seal Orchard after critical bug 

⚠️ Zcash founder Zooko Wilcox has explained how the network’s July 28 Ironwood hard fork will address uncertainty around a critical flaw in the Orchard shielded pool. The upgrade will not identify or freeze individual counterfeit coins. Instead, it will seal the old pool and limit how much ZEC can leave. 

🔖 Ironwood, also known as NU6.3, is scheduled to activate at block 3,428,143 on July 28. The upgrade will retire the current Orchard pool and introduce a new shielded pool based on the corrected circuit. According to Zcash’s official Ironwood user update, users will no longer be able to send or receive ZEC inside the old Orchard pool after activation. Funds can leave only through the turnstile, which prevents more ZEC from exiting than legitimately entered.

⭐️ The Zcash team said it believes the flaw was “unlikely to have been exploited,” but users cannot independently prove no counterfeit ZEC was created. Ironwood aims to trap any excess value inside the old pool rather than allow it to enter wider circulation. Security researcher Taylor Hornby discovered the Orchard flaw on May 29 while auditing the shielded system. The bug could have allowed an attacker to create counterfeit ZEC inside Orchard without leaving an obvious public record.

India’s main opposition Congress party had also seized upon the mood, calling for Modi to resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth” as it held its own protest in Delhi on Tuesday.

While the CJP movement has primarily focused on accountability for devastating leaks of exam papers and calling for the resignation of the education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, the overriding feeling in the aftermath of Monday’s protest was that this was now so much bigger than one issue. For some, this was the moment India’s youth – totalling more than 600 million – had found its political voice.

“The solidarity on the streets yesterday filled my heart,” 
said Kuhoo Kaushik, 26, a content creator from Delhi. 
“How the government responded was really sad, police beating up 14-year-olds is horrible. But personally, I feel like it’s really awoken something in me.

“That’s why I’ve come back today: we won’t be moved until the government listens to us. It’s become about so much more than education – but one step at a time”’

Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke vowed that the protests would continue, though did not state what the next steps for the movement would be to capitalise on their momentum.

Standing by the stage at the protest site, Ratna Singh, a CJP spokesperson, said the movement was very aware of ways in which the Modi government had successfully cracked down on previous movements and figures of dissent during its 12 years in power.

“Anyone who has tried to speak up against this government has faced terrorism charges or tax raids or jail and there is so much fear,” 
she said. 
“But I am very proud at how many people have showed up and come out on the streets. The police showed us no mercy – but no matter what barbaric treatment they give us, we will not be silenced.”

While a senior government minister met two CJP spokespeople on Monday to discuss their demands, Singh said the government had not responded to them on Tuesday and the “prime minister has remained silent about what happened”.

It was not only young people who returned to the protest site on Tuesday. Shobha Varma, 80, was attending with her granddaughter. 

“Our education system has been failing young people for years,”
 she said. 
“But when I look out at everyone here, I really feel hope.”
